subject: Post-demo recap & benchmark plan: StreamlineAI latency challenge
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@streamlineai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & benchmark plan: StreamlineAI latency challenge

Hi Elena — great conversation today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move the latency/throughput evaluation forward.

What we heard (high level)
- Primary objective: prove sub-100ms p95 for short interactive prompts (<= 512 tokens) and measure tokens/sec at sustained loads for batch/throughput scenarios.
- Concern: current hyperscaler endpoints show 20–40% variance at p99 during spikes; you want predictable tail behavior.
- Constraints: production-like payloads, red-team prompts excluded, data residency: US only.

How Redwood differs (short)
- Smart routing + prefix KV cache reduces repeated-token costs and lowers p95 for conversational workloads.
- Quantization profiles tuned for the model family you demoed keep throughput higher while maintaining quality.
- Built-in fallbacks allow us to degrade to a lower-cost variant automatically during sustained overloads.

Proposed A/B test matrix (attached as connor_benchmark_matrix.xlsx) — summary
- Tests: 1) Interactive latency (single-stream, 1–8 concurrent users) at 128/512 token lengths; 2) Throughput runs (tokens/sec) at 50/200/500 parallel streams for 10 minutes; 3) Tail-run (p99) with synthetic burst patterns to mimic chat spikes.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, median tokens/sec, 95th percentile CPU/GPU utilization, error rate, and cost per 1M tokens.
- Comparison points: your current hyperscaler baseline (you provided baseline data today) and the Redwood hosted endpoint.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you share the 2 representative prompt sets you mentioned (interactive + bulk) and a small sample payload (10–20 items)?
2) Please introduce us to your infra lead (for network egress configs) — cc’ing a placeholder for now.
3) Do you want Redwood to run tests in your account (private deployment) or on our hosted endpoints? We recommend host + private A/B for identical infra conditions; see matrix for pros/cons.

Timeline
- If we get payloads + infra contact by EOD Friday (Aug 6), we can run a first pass by the week of Aug 10 and share results the week after.

Attachments: connor_benchmark_matrix.xlsx (xlsx) — matrix + sample CLI commands; redwood-vs-hyperscaler-latency-notes.pdf (pdf) — quick differentiators doc.

Thanks — I’ll hold a 30min slot on Monday to review the test plan if that works for you.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Marissa / Vivek — forwarding Elena's reply and the sample payloads she attached. Quick internal plan and asks so we can move fast:

1) Runner environment: we should provision a Redwood hosted dedicated endpoint for the initial run (keeps variables low). If results look good, we'll spin up a private VPC run in their account for the A/B. Vivek, can you spin up a short-lived dedicated pool (1x A10G equivalent) and share endpoint + auth by EOD Thu?

2) Test harness: use the attached connor_benchmark_matrix.xlsx. TL;DR: interactive (128/512 tokens) 3x 10-min runs at 1/4/8 concurrency; throughput: 3x 10-min runs at 50/200/500 streams. Collect p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec.

3) Controls & audit: Elena asked for a one-pager for their audit team. I started a draft in the shared Drive link (see related_links). Can one of you quick-review and add the security controls and IP ranges we will use?

4) Reporting: deliverable is a short slide deck + CSV with raw runs, plus a 1-pager summary. Marissa, can you own the post-run analysis and the deck? I’ll own the customer write-up and next-step ask.

Attachments referenced: connor_benchmark_matrix.xlsx, redwood-vs-hyperscaler-latency-notes.pdf

Connor

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 09:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Post-demo recap & benchmark plan: StreamlineAI latency challenge

Connor / Vivek — quick confirmation and additions:

- I’ll own analysis and the deliverable deck. Plan to run the k6-based harness described in the matrix.
- Execution plan (short):
  * Interactive latency: 3 runs each at concurrency [1,4,8], durations 10m; collect p50/p95/p99 for 128/512 token sizes.
  * Throughput: 3 runs each at streams [50,200,500], 10m steady-state; measure tokens/sec and error tails.
  * Tail stress: 2x 5-minute burst runs (sine + Poisson bursts) to capture p99 under intermittent spikes.
- Observation windows: we’ll capture GPU utilization (nvidia-smi) and VM-level metrics at 10s granularity.
- Expected outputs: CSVs (raw), aggregated metrics JSON, slide deck summary.

Vivek — please confirm the dedicated pool onboarding ETA (EOD Thu would be ideal). I’ll start a draft of the one-pager for StreamlineAI’s audit team and drop it in the Drive folder; Connor, will add the commercial/SLAs section.

Marissa
